outcome: A permanent with hexproof is not a legal target for spells and abilities its controller's opponents control, both when targets are chosen and when they are rechecked on resolution.
A player with hexproof is not a legal target for spells and abilities their opponents control.
A permanent with hexproof from a quality is not a legal target for opposing spells with that quality or opposing abilities from sources with it, and stays targetable by everything else.
Effects that remove hexproof or let a player ignore it apply to hexproof from a quality too, so the permanent becomes a legal target.
Hexproof from two qualities blocks opposing spells and sources of either quality.
Hexproof from each color blocks every opposing colored spell or source and leaves colorless ones able to target.

note: Redundancy of instances has no separate outcome.
